extracted.intended_audience: NIH K01 reviewers, mentoring committee members, and career-development grant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: A mentored K01 career development (K) award application proposing training and research in pediatric metabolomics to generate preliminary data and prepare the candidate to submit an R01 by year 4. Emphasizes mentorship, training plan, preliminary data, methods, and timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined mentoring committee with documented expertise and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentoring Team and Collaborators: My mentorship team includes prominent researchers in their respective fields. Each has strong records of publication, funding and mentoring (Table 1 and Mentor Statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe named mentors, their institutions, associated aims/training goals, meeting frequency and format, area of expertise and specific role (e.g., primary mentor for pneumonia, statistical mentor for cluster analysis). Include evidence of established relationships and regular meetings (weekly, monthly, quarterly) to ensure progress toward training goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear plan for transition to independence and R01 submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to Generate R01 Support: I propose to submit my first R01 by year 4 of this award (Figure 1) and gain independence from my mentorship team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concrete timeline and milestones showing how K01 activities will lead to an R01 (e.g., years 1–3: training and pilot data; year 4: design and submit R01). State how the K award will develop skills needed for independent investigator status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific, measurable career development and training goals tied to key individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Goals: GOAL 1: Gain experiential learning in study design and execution of quantitative 1H-NMR metabolomics; GOAL 2: Acquire and apply advanced statistical analytics; GOAL 3: Interpret metabolomics data and its biological context; GOAL 4: Develop leadership and professional skills to execute multicenter studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List discrete training goals with associated key mentors, specific activities (hands-on assays, courses, externships), and expected competencies. Tie each goal to named mentors and concrete learning experiences (e.g., Chenomx software, Structural Equation Modeling course, LC/MS externship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed timeline/milestones for training, research, and teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 2: Timeline of future training, research and clinical work (shows pre-K01 through Year 4–5 training months, courses, experiential learning, research aims timing, IRB submission, teaching months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a calendarized timeline showing months devoted to training, coursework, hands-on learning, research aims, IRB submission, and teaching responsibilities. Include expected time per activity and sequencing across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data demonstrating feasibility and prior cohort enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary data: Over the past 3 years, we enrolled 169 children between 3 months and 11 years of age with CAP. Preliminary NMR data suggest distinct urine metabolite profiles cluster by class of pathogen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present prior cohort size, enrollment metrics, and initial analytic results (figures such as PLS-DA, radar plots, identified metabolites) to justify feasibility and provide pilot data for aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-articulated Specific Aims with testable hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims: 1) characterize sources of variability in urine metabolite profiles of healthy children; 2) determine and compare urine metabolite profiles of children with viral or bacterial CAP vs healthy controls; 3) evaluate longitudinal changes in urine metabolite profiles of children with CAP compared with healthy children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State concise aims with primary and secondary hypotheses linked to study design and future aims (e.g., informing R01 application). Ensure aims are measurable and directly address the stated overall objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance — demonstrate unmet clinical need and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance: There is no current single test differentiating viral from bacterial CAP in children; biomarkers are insensitive and current practice leads to empiric antibiotics, overtreatment, and antibiotic resistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the clinical problem, public health impact, limitations of current diagnostics, and how the proposed work addresses an important unmet need with potential to change practice (e.g., develop non-invasive point-of-care diagnostics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation — novel approach and advantages of selected platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation: Uses an unbiased approach that integrates robust clinical phenotype data with quantitative NMR metabolomics and novel statistical methods; advantages of NMR include rapid results (<1 hour), non-invasive urine testing, and simple processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight novelty in methods, integration of datasets, translational potential, and specific technical advantages of chosen platforms (NMR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an existing, well-characterized cohort and biorepository
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Research Design: MEEP is part of CARPE DIEM, a fully-funded, operational prospective cohort with specimen banking and external funding supporting recruitment through 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage established cohorts and biobanks; describe cohort enrollment, specimen types, completeness of covariates, and how the existing infrastructure supports study aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed specimen collection, processing, and storage protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample Collection and Storage: NP swabs placed in viral transport medium and STGG and frozen at -80°C; urine collected in cups coated with 10% sodium azide, centrifuged for 10 minutes, aliquoted into 1 mL cryovials and stored at -80°C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include stepwise specimen handling protocols (collection containers, preservatives, centrifugation, aliquoting, storage temperature) to ensure sample integrity and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-analytic quality control steps for NMR (pH adjustment, internal standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before NMR: pH measured and adjusted to 7.0 ± 0.25 if necessary; add 10% volume equivalent of DSS as internal standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify pre-analytic QC measures such as pH normalization and internal standard use to standardize spectra across samples and runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit NMR acquisition and processing parameters and software
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquire one-dimensional 1H-NMR spectra using the NOESY pulse sequence on Varian Inova-500 MHz or Bruker 600 MHz; spectra processed using Chenomx (NMR Suite 8.0) including referencing, shimming, phasing, baseline correction, identification and quantification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide instrument models, pulse sequences, acquisition temperatures, and software/workflow for spectrum processing to allow replication and evaluation of analytic rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of analytically significant metabolites via orthogonal methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity of any statistically significant metabolites will be confirmed by 2D NMR; low abundance (<5 µM) or significant compounds will also undergo analytical confirmation using LC/MS with Dr. Ziady.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan confirmatory analyses (2D NMR, LC/MS) for key findings and low-abundance metabolites to ensure analytic validity and reduce false positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random batching and de-identification to minimize batch effects and bias
rubrics_metrics.description: De-identified samples (n=50) will be shipped frozen; case and control samples will be randomly batched and processed to minimize artificial effects arising from day-to-day variation in NMR runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement de-identification, random batching, and standardized shipping/storage to control for batch and timing artifacts; describe batching strategy and its rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization and inclusion thresholds for metabolite data
rubrics_metrics.description: Before statistical analyses, quantified NMR metabolite data will be normalized to account for the influence of metabolites present in either high or low concentrations. Only metabolites that are reported in at least 90% of the samples will be included in the analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify normalization approaches and clear inclusion criteria (e.g., ≥90% detection) to limit analyses to reliable metabolites and reduce analytic noise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plan with appropriate models for variability and longitudinal data
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical Analysis: descriptive statistics and graphics; metabolite concentrations transformed if necessary; estimate between-subject and within-subject variability using linear mixed models with random effect for subject and time nested within subject; estimate ICC and include fixed effects for age and sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe analytic methods matched to study aims (mixed models for repeated measures/variance components, transformations for normality, ICC estimation) and specify covariates to be tested (age, sex).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple testing correction strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: To account for multiple testing due to metabolites from the same child we will use false discovery rate procedures, such as the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare the method for controlling type I error across many metabolites (e.g., FDR), and indicate thresholds or reporting plans for significant findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power and sample size justification tied to detectable effect sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample Size: log-normal power analysis for differences in metabolite concentrations; with planned enrollment of 125 healthy controls (110 providing ≥3 samples) we estimate 80% power to detect a geometric mean ratio of 1.38 assuming CV=0.5 and p<0.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide analytic assumptions (CV, alpha), planned sample numbers, expected detectable effect sizes, and power calculations tied to primary outcomes; explain how enrollment targets relate to power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned handling of missing data and sensitivity/subanalyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential missingness: from preliminary data 7/50 metabolites had random missing patterns; as a subanalysis we will impute missing concentration if metabolite has between 10–30% missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State thresholds for imputation vs exclusion, the imputation approach and planned sensitivity analyses to assess impact of missingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management and database plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Management: Clinical data extracted from Epic and imported into REDCap; metabolomics data expressed as one record per study ID per identified metabolite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe data provenance, database systems, record structure, and data linkage procedures to ensure integrity, reproducibility, and auditability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of core facilities, external labs, and collaborative resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens shipped to University of Michigan NMR Metabolomics Laboratory; specimen processing and storage facilitated by the Cincinnati BioBank Core Facility (CBCF); collaborations with Drs. Stringer, Romick-Rosendale, Ziady, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional cores and external collaborators with specific roles (assays, externships, analytic expertise), letters of support, and plans for cross-center validation and training exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay reproducibility strategies including technical replicates and cross-center validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy: run technical replicates of the same samples in the newly established metabolomics core laboratory at CCHMC to ensure reproducibility and enable independent assay of remaining samples; gain understanding of cross-center NMR validation studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for technical replicates, inter-lab comparison, and procedures to assess assay reproducibility and platform concordance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated outcomes and linkage to future grant plans and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected Outcomes: generate preliminary data on distinct metabolite profiles associated with bacterial and viral pneumonia to inform an R01 for large multi-center validation and development of point-of-care tests; present findings at national/international meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State expected deliverables (pilot data, validated profiles), planned dissemination venues (conferences), and how results will feed into future grant submissions (R01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit rationale for aim-level methods and selection of timepoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 1 rationale: choose three time points (T0, T1 24 hours, T2 14 days) to demonstrate acute changes in the metabolome; rationale cites prior pediatric literature sparsity and adult findings on between- vs within-subject variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify sampling schedule and analytic approach in the context of biological mechanisms and prior literature; link timepoints to specific hypotheses about magnitude/duration of metabolome changes.
